dimensions.routes_to: the JUDGE, not an acquisition and not a specialist
dimensions.justification: Appendix R3: BLOCKED means no artefact we have can measure it, not 'the instrument I built cannot'. The overlay _jn12seg-nickel-rev-proof.png shows all seven thresholds' contours running along Monticello's own dome, pediment, portico, wings, terrace and end pavilions, tight to the building and — unlike the quarter's eagle — NOT welded to either legend. Nearly all of the 0.164 of disagreement is INTERIOR holes in the frosting, not silhouette. Two pieces of judge work would settle it and neither needs a photograph: (1) fill interior holes, which _nkseg.segment() already does and _jq43seg.motif() does not; (2) run the light-field references in the opposite polarity. The nickel is much closer to a frozen reverse target than the quarter ever got.

dimensions.name: structural rhythm at the icon tier
dimensions.metric: same
dimensions.justification: At icon the drawing deliberately substitutes ONE lit block for the four-column portico, on the documented ground that 'three field-coloured slots at 23px are stripes, not a portico' (§15.4). That decision is reasoned and it is in the source; it has never been SCORED, and §15.4's own title is 'the rhythm must survive the tier drop'. It is recorded as a miss rather than exempted, because §8 forbids writing an exemption after seeing the value. What the round can say is that a reader should treat this as a design decision to re-examine, not as a bug.

dimensions.metric: rim seat = the innermost radius outboard of the legend at which the along-angle MEAN grey falls more than 25 levels below the field level (median mean over r 41..43)
dimensions.locus: whole circle; search window r 42.0..46.5; both bounds printed

dimensions.excluded: nickel-obv-proof.png (45.70) and nickel-rev-proof.png (43.20) are excluded: this rule is PHOTOMETRIC and a cameo proof's field is a black mirror (§20.3/§20.4). They are also one photograph, not two.
dimensions.corroboration: The quarter's round 4 measured its own rim seat at 44.2 on three references by a completely different method (a viewBox ladder read by eye off a polar unwrap). Two coins, two methods, 44.33 and 44.2 — 0.13 units apart.
dimensions.consequence: The coin gives its legend 44.33 - 36.8 = 7.53 units of band. We give it 41.0 - 36.4 = 4.60. That is why D5-cap cannot be fixed by a specialist working inside `EDGE`: growing the cap to the coin's ~5.8 puts the cap box outside the field circle and converts a lettering failure into a D8 containment failure. It is the identical wall the quarter hit (7.7 vs 4.6).

dimensions.name: edge quality
dimensions.metric: width-variation ratio per mark (a stroke-rendered mark is 1.000 by construction); FRACTION OF DRAWN LENGTH carried by ratio-1.000 marks. Lettering, the blank, the two field circles and the specular arc excluded by name.
dimensions.gate: BASELINE, NO GATE. §3 says D6's gate is 'declared per coin' and no declaration has ever been written for any coin.
dimensions.justification: The metric §3 asks for had never been implemented — `_jq67edge.mjs` still runs the bounding-box neighbour test that Appendix P1 SUPERSEDED, and on the nickel it duly flags 10 of 10 and 17 of 17 stroke marks, which cannot rank and cannot route. `_jn13d6.mjs` implements the adopted metric. It ranks: the dime, whose jaw line §14 names as the known instance, reads 24.9% and 35.2% against the nickel's 11.7% and 15.9%. The value exists; the per-coin gate the rubric requires does not, and inventing one now, after the value, is what §8 forbids.

dimensions.name: curve quality
dimensions.metric: max knot turn. §3 as revised by Appendix P2: FITTED CONTOURS ONLY; a path authored as a polygon declares its corners in the scorecard, by index, and a path with NO DECLARATION IS SCORED WHOLE.
dimensions.locus: every scored path in the shipped SVG at 190 px
dimensions.justification: On the fitted contours alone the nickel obverse passes at 71.5 degrees, comfortably. It fails because P2's exemption is conditional on a DECLARATION that does not exist: no corner declaration has ever been written, for this coin or any other, so 'a path with no declaration is scored whole' applies and the three authored paths above are in scope. The repair is cheap and is not art: write the declaration. The list above is it.

dimensions.name: containment
dimensions.metric: % of drawn path length outside EDGE.nickel.field[tier], AND deepest breach in viewBox units
dimensions.locus: EDGE.nickel.field[tier]; the full candidate circle set is printed on every row and reads `47(blank,rejected) 40.5(fill) 40.5(ring)`
dimensions.gate: 0.00% at every tier; a breach shallower than 0.01 units (n2()'s quantum) is reported at its depth and does not count
dimensions.diagnosis: Two separate offenders, and only one of them is the bevel. (1) HEAD.Jefferson's own outline reaches r 40.640 BEFORE any offset — 0.1398 units outside the mid field circle of 40.5, on 3.74 units of length per copy. (2) `bust()` emits two offset copies of the same path at translate(-+ro) with NO bound, and that carries the lit copy to 41.970 — a breach of 1.4698 units on 22.17 units of length. `struck()` already bounds the reverse's offset with `fitOff(o, solid, rField)`; `bust()` does not, and `src/art/coins.js:3307-3313` says so in its own comment. Both fixes are small and neither needs the head redrawn from scratch.
dimensions.response_test: the instrument's own RESPONSE=1 moves a mark 20 units outward and the fraction goes from 0 to clearly non-zero (validated on the quarter at this hash).

dimensions.what_the_control_settled: I went in holding three numbers of my own manufacture that all say 'the nickel obverse is a dark blob'. The dime control is EQUALLY dark at 26 px, so 'inky icon portrait' is a property of bust() and the palette and is not attributable to the nickel. What the control does NOT show, and the nickel does, is the head crossing and interrupting the pale rim ring on the left at 26 and 44 px — which is D8's 1.47 units, visible. The vertical seam artefact in the 26 px panels appears in the control too and is my sheet's, not the art's.

dimensions.metric: mean/field and ink fraction over the disc interior, ours vs ref/nickel-obv.jpg reduced to the SAME device pixel count, each normalised by its own p90 field
dimensions.locus: r < 40 (whole interior) and r < 33 (inside every legend, §22.8)
dimensions.note: Outside the gate at every tier, in the same direction: our obverse is far too dark and carries roughly TWICE the ink the coin does. The RAD-33 rows at 26 and 44 px are NOT used: the instrument's own §22.1 assert fired, recovering field levels of 210 and 180 instead of the palette's 212, because at that radius and that device pixel count the p90 no longer lands on bare field. Reporting the assert rather than the number is the point of having it.

The ink fraction is short by 0.09-0.15 at every tier, and a large part of that shortfall is the legend we do not draw (D5-presence): at RAD 33, inside every legend, the ink gap halves to -0.045/-0.061/-0.087.
